description: Israel licensed Jawwal just 4.8 MHz in the 900 MHz band in 1999. Jawwal retained that same allocation while its subscriber base grew from 120,000 to more than 2.5 million, limited to a 2G system with mobile internet over EDGE.
energy_note: Twenty times the users, the same sliver of air.

aspect: 3G arrived twelve years late, and not everywhere
description: Israel launched 3G in 2004 and blocked Palestinian access to the frequencies for nearly twelve years. In November 2015 it agreed to allow 3G in the West Bank only; it launched in January 2018. Israel had already granted 4G licences to six Israeli operators in 2015. Gaza has only ever had 2G.
energy_note: A generation of technology, withheld for twelve years.

aspect: The second operator never reached Gaza at all
description: Wataniya won a combined 2G/3G licence in 2006 with a $354 million bid, received it in March 2007, and could not launch commercially in the West Bank until November 2009. It was never able to begin operations in Gaza because of restrictions on spectrum and imports, leaving Gaza a monopoly market.
energy_note: Paid $354 million for a licence it couldn't use.

description: The World Bank found the Palestinian mobile sector lost over $1 billion in potential earnings across three years, largely from Israeli restrictions, with over 20% of West Bank customers using Israeli providers for speed.
energy_note: A billion dollars, in three years, in a small economy.

aspect: Slow networks exclude people from the modern economy
description: Remote work, online study, telemedicine, e-government and digital payments all assume bandwidth. A 2G household is excluded from each of them regardless of the person's skills.
energy_note: Qualified for the remote job, and unable to join the call.

aspect: And the network you do have routes through the other side
description: Both operators license spectrum from the Israeli government, route traffic through Israel, and must use an Israeli-registered company for international links. EFF noted that with Palestinian telcos locked to less secure 2G, interception is easier even for users of Palestinian carriers.
energy_note: Your call is carried by the people you're hiding from.

aspect: EXAMPLE - a $354 million licence that could not be used

energy_note: Three hundred and fifty-four million dollars, for a network in one half of a territory.
